title: Define DatasetDesignV1
problem: Current command sequences do not preserve one product-level statement of row grain, feature meaning, missing meaning, and loss policy
change: Add a closed DatasetDesignV1 with row grain, feature definition, role, missing meaning, and root-value source
acceptance: A valid Patient plus Gender design round-trips, receives a stable digest, and rejects paths, recipes, expressions, or unknown variants
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/datasetdesign/... ./internal/explorer/authoringv2/...
observed_verification: Authoring V2 already has typed source and command unions but no dataset design boundary
migration: New wizard datasets use design version 1; existing V2 drafts remain on the current path

title: Lower a root-value design through the current compiler
problem: A new product type is useful only if it reuses the proven receipt and compiler path
change: Add one validated design-to-V2 adapter for Patient grain and root-value features; retain the normalized design and digest in the receipt
acceptance: Patient ID and Gender compile to the same literal Preview rows as ordinary V2 fields under one immutable receipt
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/datasetdesign/... ./internal/explorer/compilation/...
observed_verification: The compiler already accepts field sources and emits receipt contracts
migration: Keep the existing V2 compiler authoritative; do not create a second query engine

title: Create the Rows step and Patient choice
problem: The current graph asks users to choose a technical root without presenting the row-grain consequence
change: Add a Rows step with the prompt What should one row represent and a Patient card labeled One row for each patient
acceptance: The live DOM at [data-testid=rows-step] shows One row per Patient; [data-testid=row-grain-patient] selects Patient ID and enables Continue without requiring the graph view
verification_command: cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard; make verify-fast
observed_verification: Builder already creates a local table and emits CREATE_TABLE after root selection
migration: Ship the wizard behind a per-Explorer flag; retain the graph as Advanced

title: Measure Patient row-key integrity and Gender coverage safely
problem: A declared row grain is not trustworthy without measured null and duplicate keys, and sampled or incomplete evidence must not look complete
change: Add receipt-bound evidence with snapshot, generation, limits, completeness, total rows, null keys, duplicate keys, populated values, and missing values
acceptance: [data-testid=row-key-evidence] reports rows 2, nullKeys 0, duplicateKeys 0, Gender populated 1, Gender missing 1, complete true, and the same receipt as full Preview; incomplete evidence cannot report ready
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/lifecycle/... ./internal/server; cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard
observed_verification: Preview returns columns and rows but no measured key, coverage, limits, or completeness evidence
migration: Version the evidence response; unknown, truncated, stale, or failed measurement stays explicit and fails closed

title: Add Gender as the first useful feature
problem: The first package must deliver a useful feature, not only infrastructure or a row-grain label
change: Add an A value flow for Patient Gender with a feature card, inline sample, coverage, and full Preview action
acceptance: [data-feature-key=gender] says Gender and 50% populated; [data-testid=feature-preview] and full Preview map dev-patient-001 to female and dev-patient-002 to null under one receipt
verification_command: cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard FeatureEditor; make verify-fast
observed_verification: The browser driver already creates Patient fields and asserts the exact two Preview rows
migration: New wizard state is isolated by the Explorer flag; current ColumnSelector remains available in Advanced

title: Add the hostile related-record fixture and preserve the current journey
problem: The fast fixture does not contain two related Observations for one Patient and cannot expose silent relationship collapse
change: Add one preliminary Observation for Patient 001 and extend the existing driver without replacing its Preview, Publish, Viewer, CSV, or reload checks
acceptance: Patient 001 has two Observations and Patient 002 has one; authoring and Preview share one receipt, publish records the revision from that receipt, and Viewer plus CSV use the returned materialization selector
verification_command: node --test scripts/loom-dev.test.mjs; make dev-doctor && make verify-fast; make verify-full
observed_verification: The current driver proves the mechanical end-to-end flow and the fixture has only two Observations
migration: Keep existing resource IDs stable and add the new record explicitly

title: Add the closed related-feature source union
problem: Aggregate and related source types exist below the UI but no durable product command authors their meaning
change: Add related-value, related-count, and related-exists variants plus one Observation-status predicate to DatasetDesignV1
acceptance: The API accepts only the named variants and observation-status-is predicate and rejects arbitrary equality, generic Coding filters, expressions, latest, units, and time windows
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/datasetdesign/... ./internal/explorer/authoringv2/...
observed_verification: Authoring V2 and compilation already model aggregates and primitive where-path equality
migration: Version the source union and migrate all wizard callers in the same package

title: Expose observed relationship multiplicity
problem: A scalar child field can silently take the first related resource because route multiplicity is absent from authoring evidence
change: Extend receipt-bound evidence with none, one, many, maximum, and affected-root counts for the selected route
acceptance: [data-testid=route-cardinality] reports none 0, one 1, many 1 before the related value can be saved
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/compilation/... ./internal/dataframe/compiler/... ./internal/explorer/lifecycle/...
observed_verification: The compiler currently reduces direct child scalar fields with FIRST over a flattened child set
migration: Legacy unknown multiplicity remains explicit and cannot become safe by default

title: Author Observation count
problem: Researchers cannot create a basic related-record count through Builder
change: Add the A count card and lower unfiltered related count to the existing COUNT aggregate
acceptance: [data-feature-key=observation_count] and [data-testid=feature-preview] show 2 for Patient 001 and 1 for Patient 002; full Preview, GraphQL, Viewer, and CSV agree
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/... ./internal/dataframe/compiler/...; cd ui && npm test -- FeatureEditor; make verify-fast
observed_verification: The compiler supports COUNT but the visible UI submits only field sources
migration: Retain existing pre-authored aggregate documents and add the wizard command as a typed caller

title: Author Observation-status count and yes-or-no features
problem: Counts alone do not let a researcher express a small useful condition over related Observations
change: Add one Observation status picker and lower status-filtered COUNT and EXISTS through WherePath and WhereEquals
acceptance: [data-feature-key=final_observation_count] shows 1 and 1; [data-feature-key=has_preliminary_observation] shows true and false; full Preview, GraphQL, Viewer, and CSV agree
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/... ./internal/dataframe/compiler/lower/...; cd ui && npm test -- FeatureEditor; make verify-fast
observed_verification: The backend has aggregate and primitive equality vocabulary but no guided UI authoring path
migration: The predicate remains Observation status only; do not accept arbitrary field equality or require a Coding system

title: Require an explicit related-value policy
problem: A related scalar is unsafe when the route has many matches and INDEXED does not solve cross-resource multiplicity
change: Offer require-one, keep-all, or acknowledged first-by-resource-id; refuse require-one when evidence contains many and block publication if later data violates it
acceptance: [data-testid=related-value-save] stays disabled for require-one with many; [data-testid=lossy-feature-warning] reports one dropped value for acknowledged first and the receipt says lossless false; later invariant violation emits RELATIONSHIP_CARDINALITY_VIOLATION
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/... ./internal/dataframe/compiler/...; cd ui && npm test -- FeatureEditor; make verify-fast
observed_verification: Current compilation classifies field repetition but not relationship multiplicity
migration: Legacy related FIRST remains readable in the legacy flow and unresolved in the wizard

title: Make each feature card explain and preview itself
problem: Users must not switch to a contract screen or decode FHIR paths to understand one feature
change: Render inline values, coverage, warning state, and a How this is made disclosure from the receipt feature descriptor
acceptance: Each [data-feature-key] card shows its literal sample and coverage; [data-testid=feature-lineage] shows resource, relationship, exact path, Observation status filter, operation, missing meaning, and stable key
verification_command: cd ui && npm test -- FeatureEditor DataframeContractPanel; make verify-fast
observed_verification: Runtime types carry partial lineage and the contract panel renders path-oriented metadata
migration: Use one versioned descriptor and keep exact paths as advanced evidence

title: Refresh Check after every design repair
problem: A repair changes the design and receipt, so retaining prior evidence would show results for the wrong rows or features
change: Invalidate evidence on every design edit and run Check only for the newly reconciled receipt; reject stale response identities
acceptance: [data-testid=readiness-state] clears after a repair, then names the new receipt after Check; stale or incomplete evidence cannot enable [data-testid=publish-dataset]
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/lifecycle/... ./internal/server; cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard
observed_verification: F1 introduces receipt identity and completeness; Builder already reconciles a new receipt before Preview and publish
migration: Keep evidence keyed by receipt and output; never migrate cached results between receipts

title: Measure feature coverage, shape, and bounded distribution
problem: Sample cells do not reveal all-null, sparse, constant, or unexpectedly high-cardinality features
change: Run bounded profiling against the validated receipt through the Preview execution boundary and return populated, missing, empty, invalid, distinct, and type-appropriate range evidence
acceptance: [data-testid=quality-report] shows Gender populated 1 and missing 1, Observation count range 1 to 2, and an all-null feature at zero percent coverage under the Preview receipt
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/lifecycle/... ./internal/dataframe/compiler/... ./internal/server; cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard DataframeContractPanel
observed_verification: Builder Preview executes a validated receipt before publication; it currently returns rows without quality measurements
migration: Report unknown or truncated measurements explicitly; never query current published data or promote incomplete evidence to ready

title: Define stable readiness reasons and publication policy
problem: One ML-ready boolean hides the evidence and cannot tell the user what to repair
change: Derive ready, ready_with_warnings, or blocked from typed evidence and stable reason records with repair targets
acceptance: [data-testid=readiness-state] shows the state; each [data-reason-code] names evidence and repair; hard reasons including RELATIONSHIP_CARDINALITY_VIOLATION disable [data-testid=publish-dataset]
verification_command: go test ./internal/explorer/datasetdesign/... ./internal/explorer/lifecycle/...; cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard DataframeContractPanel
observed_verification: The current panel renders compile-time lossless and ML-ready booleans
migration: Legacy boolean-only contracts decode as unknown evidence rather than ready

title: Focus the exact control that repairs a reason
problem: A warning list without navigation still requires a nontechnical user to diagnose the implementation model
change: Add repair actions that return to Rows or Features and focus the grain control or feature card named by the reason
acceptance: Clicking [data-reason-code=ROLE_UNSPECIFIED] focuses [data-feature-key=gender]; setting role and missing meaning removes the reason, reconciles a new receipt, and requires fresh evidence
verification_command: cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard FeatureEditor DataframeContractPanel; make verify-fast
observed_verification: Builder already owns selection state and the contract panel already lists output facts
migration: Migrated features use unspecified role and unknown missing meaning and produce warnings

title: Share feature meaning and value rendering across views
problem: Builder, Preview, Viewer, and future artifacts can display different labels, nulls, arrays, and lineage for the same feature
change: Use the versioned feature descriptor and one null and array display policy in every view
acceptance: Gender, counts, yes-or-no, related arrays, nulls, and exact lineage render consistently before publish, after publish, and after reload
verification_command: go test ./internal/fhir/schema/...; cd ui && npm test -- FeatureEditor PreviewTable ExplorerViewer; make verify-fast
observed_verification: Viewer owns local value-to-text behavior and runtime types carry only partial semantic metadata
migration: Parse legacy descriptors once at the API boundary and preserve machine values separately from display text

title: Expose one public pinned artifact operation
problem: The UI CSV guard detects materialization changes, but no public server operation pins data and artifact sidecars under one identity
change: Add an authorized artifact operation that accepts and resolves one receipt, revision, output, and materialization pin before reading rows
acceptance: A real UI request starts an artifact for the exact published identity and never falls back to a current pointer
verification_command: go test ./internal/api/graphql/graph/dataframe/... ./internal/dataframe/published/... ./internal/server; make verify-fast
observed_verification: A server exporter supports text formats and the UI CSV path now guards materialization identity, but no artifact operation exists
migration: Keep Viewer CSV until its caller migrates; artifact v1 is a new operation

title: Define and assemble artifact v1
problem: A CSV alone lacks the schema, feature meaning, quality evidence, and provenance needed to reuse a training table
change: Create a versioned archive with data.csv, manifest.json, schema.json, provenance.json, quality.json, and README.md
acceptance: The archive has exactly six members; ordered descriptors, row count, quality, and identities agree across every member
verification_command: go test ./internal/dataset/... ./internal/dataframe/published/... ./internal/api/graphql/graph/dataframe/...
observed_verification: The backlog calls for data plus feature meanings but no portable artifact contract exists
migration: Artifact v1 uses CSV and has its own version independent of receipt versions

title: Stream and finalize the archive safely
problem: Browser pagination accumulates all CSV rows and a failed stream can leave ambiguous output
change: Stream rows and sidecars server-side, hash each member, and expose the download only after atomic completion
acceptance: A multi-page export keeps browser memory bounded; cancellation or a later-page failure yields no completed artifact or enabled download
verification_command: go test ./internal/api/graphql/graph/dataframe/... ./internal/dataframe/published/... ./internal/dataset/...
observed_verification: The backend can stream CSV while the UI currently builds a browser Blob
migration: Remove browser accumulation only after the new caller is live and verified

title: Add publish and artifact progress UX
problem: The current UI offers a generic CSV action without a visible immutable pin, progress, cancellation, or completeness state
change: Add Publish and export, artifact progress, cancellation, retry, failure, and completed identity controls
acceptance: [data-testid=publication-pin] names the revision and materialization; [data-testid=artifact-status] reports progress or complete; [data-testid=artifact-download] stays disabled on cancellation or failure
verification_command: cd ui && npm test -- DatasetWizard ExplorerViewer; make verify-fast
observed_verification: Publish already returns identity and Viewer already exposes CSV download
migration: Keep Download CSV as a labeled compatibility action until all callers use artifacts

title: Prove republish, failure, and checksum safety live
problem: The current CSV identity guard does not prove that a future multi-file artifact stays consistent or that a partial archive remains unavailable
change: Extend the existing live driver to unpack the archive, verify every checksum and identity, publish B during export A, and inject a later-page failure
acceptance: Every artifact A member remains A and every SHA-256 matches; after failure [data-testid=artifact-status] reports failed, [data-testid=artifact-download] stays disabled, and no complete file exists
verification_command: node --test scripts/loom-dev.test.mjs; make dev-doctor && make verify-fast
observed_verification: The driver proves Viewer CSV and reload, and the CSV path detects publication changes; no server artifact test exists
migration: Use fixture-only identities and fault injection; do not mutate production data
